test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 Quant Previous Year Paper (Held On: 8 Aug 2022)
subject: general
question: A person sells an article for a loss of 18 percent. If he increases the selling price by Rs. 144 and decreases the cost price by 30 percent, then there is profit of 20 percent. What is the original selling price ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume original CP = 100 units.

Original SP = 100 − 18 = 82 units.

New CP = 100 − 30% = 70 units.

New SP = 120% of 70 = 84 units.

Difference in SP = 84 − 82 = 2 units → Rs. 144.

1 unit = 72 ∴ Original SP = 82 × 72 = Rs. 5904.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5904.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial loss = 18%

Increase in SP = Rs. 144

Decrease in CP = 30%

Final Profit = 20%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e433ef5db552f61664cb20ab440296e91a785f1d20be592c8d3629f7e210cb31.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the original cost price be 100x.

⇒ Original Selling Price = 100x − 18% of 100x = 82x

⇒ New Cost Price = 100x − 30% of 100x = 70x

⇒ New Selling Price = 70x + 20% of 70x

⇒ New Selling Price = 70x + 14x = 84x

⇒ Difference in Selling Prices = New SP − Original SP

⇒ 84x − 82x = 144

⇒ 2x = 144

⇒ x = 72

⇒ Original Selling Price = 82x = 82 × 72

⇒ Original Selling Price = Rs. 5904

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 5904.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Basic Formulas

Profit = SP − CP; Loss = CP − SP. Profit% = (Profit/CP) × 100; Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

SP = Marked Price − Discount. Discount% = (Discount/MP) × 100.

Selling Price for Profit/Loss

SP = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100 or SP = CP × (100 − Loss%)/100.</p
